items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Bob Haggart and I had done so many things that Bob Crosby got credit for, that we want to get together and organize a group. And was I interested. ... Hank came in one night and said he was doing a Show of Shows... Now we get to the Lawson-Haggart band

ctx.x: I made some recordings that were great sellers, but you know, they were in the commercial vein, too, like being on staff at Decca Records, I recorded "Lover" with Peggy Lee, and I made a Paul Whitman album with Paul in attendance, and we featured Tom and Jimmie Dorsey -- his life -- that's what Whitman was setting up in the album. And I appeared with Bob Crosby's Bobcats at the Rainbow Grill in Manhattan and the Riviera in Las Vegas -- that was my first time in Vegas. That was a beautiful experience. In the late…

Now we get to the Lawson-Haggart band, and my expression comes to the forefront, my expression -- a musical romance. Well, it certainly was. Yank Lawson, who I knew, had associated with -- in Tommy Dorsey's, he was in that great band along with Pee Wee Irwin in '39. Now, just as I was finishing up in Nick's, Hank came in one night and said he was doing a Show of Shows, and he was on the outside, to make some money. He was doing the Show of Shows, and he said
Bob Haggart and I had done so many things that Bob Crosby got credit for, that we want to get together and organize a group. And was I interested.
